chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, and others, from Sahl ibnarrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group from our companions who gather and prayer time arrives, so some of them say to others, 'Proceed, O so-and-so.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The people should be led in prayer by the one who is most proficient in reciting the Quran. If they are equal in recitation, then the one who migrated earlier. If they are equal in migration, then the eldest in age. If they are equal in age, then let the one most knowledgeable of the Sunnah and most understanding of the Religion lead them. And none of you should proceed to lead the man in his house, nor the one in authority in his domain.'

key_terms.هِجْرَةً: Migration (specifically from Mecca to Medina, used as a chronological marker)

ai.seo_question: What is the order of priority for choosing the person to lead congregational prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the classical Shia hierarchy for selecting an Imam, prioritizing Quranic proficiency, then Hijrah, age, and finally jurisprudential knowledge (Fiqh), reflecting the scholarly emphasis on both ritual excellence and doctrinal understanding. It further clarifies that this hierarchy applies to communal settings, preventing a senior individual from imposing leadership in his own home or domain against the consensus of residents, thereby preserving social harmony and the rights of the community.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, and someone else, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the people from our companions gathering, and the Salāt presents itself. So some of them are saying to the others, ‘Proceed, O so and so (to lead Salāt)’. So heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘He would proceed (to lead) the people, the one who is the most read (well-versed) of the Quran. And if they were equal in their recitation, so the first one to have migrated. And if they were equal in their migration (from Makkah to Al-Medina), so their eldest one in age. And if they were of equal ages, so let the most knowledgeable of them in the Sunnah lead them (in Salāt) and the one who is the most understanding of them in the Religion; and not one of you should proceed (to lead in Salāt) the man in his house, nor the one in authority in his domain’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad and others have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu ‘Ubaydah who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a people of our companions who come together then Salah (prayer) time comes. Certain ones among them say to the others, ‘O so and so lead.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said that the most learned in al-Quran is to lead. If all of them are equally learned in al-Quran, the first to migrate among them, if all are equal in migration, then the oldest among them, if all are equal in age, then the most learned among them in the Sunnah and most learned in religion is to lead. No one of you must lead one in his house or the one with authority in his dominion.’”
